findings.headline: Enterprise guides default to the Starter allowance. Only the FAQ says so.
findings.explanation: A customer paying well above Starter, who assumed guides scaled with their contract, finds out when you ask them to get in touch.

claim_a.quote: Contact us Volume-based discounts and monthly notified user pricing available.

claim_b.quote: you'll have the same guides limit as our Starter plan: 2,500 active users a month

findings.why_not_just_wording: Contact us invites the reader to assume a negotiated number while the FAQ states a specific default equal to the tier below.
findings.caveat: The FAQ is on the same page, forty rows down, under a question aimed at existing customers rather than buyers.

findings.headline: Pricing page says triggers are unlimited. Every endpoint is rate limited.
findings.explanation: Triggering a workflow is an API call, and the tiers are never mapped to plans or endpoints.

claim_b.quote: Each endpoint in the Knock API is rate limited. Knock uses a tier system to determine the rate limit scale for each endpoint.

findings.why_not_just_wording: Unlimited triggers and a per-second ceiling answer the same buyer question with different numbers.
findings.caveat: Rate limits and volume allowances are different, and your docs invite customers to ask for more. Naming the tier for the trigger endpoint would fix it.

coverage_notes.what_was_not_checkable: We did not report the rate-limit tier table that appears on two documentation pages with different numbers in view. It is one table of endpoint scales reproduced on both pages, not two conflicting limits, and an automated reader could easily mistake it for a contradiction. We could not check which tier any given endpoint belongs to, since that mapping is not on the pages we read. Your pricing table promises unlimited feed retention while the API reference refers to data subject to deletion under the retention policy on your account. The retention policy page was not reachable from our crawl, so we could not tell whether these describe the same data and did not report it. The signup page is blocked by robots.txt, so trial and card-requirement terms were not checked.
